title: No geomagnetic-storm reduction in nocturnal bird migration over Europe: a replication with frozen analysis plans on weather-radar data, 2023-2025
contribution_type: replication with analysis plans frozen in a private repository with a negative result; technical note and reproducible evidence packet

owner.source_commit_scope: Pipeline, tests, explorations, frozen models and committed outputs as archived; packaging files (zenodo/) are committed separately afterwards.

claim: Three tests frozen before the 2023-2025 Aloft radar data were downloaded all return FAIL: a -17% storm-night (Kp >= 6-) reduction in nocturnal migration is excluded in autumn (-2.9% [95% CI -9.5, +4.1], 23 nights) and spring (+9.2% [-1.2, +20.8], 25 nights); -9% is excluded in spring (Kp >= 7-: +10.2% [-10.1, +35.0], 8 nights; Kp >= 6- 90% lower bound +0.5%). Autumn alone is only weak evidence against -9% (in VID terms it excludes about -10%). The post hoc autumn Kp >= 7- lead (-9.3%) did not replicate in spring.
predecessor_credit: Hypothesis and US effect sizes: Gulson-Castillo et al. (2023), PNAS 120:e2306317120, doi:10.1073/pnas.2306317120. Data: Aloft (CC0; Desmet et al. 2025) and EUMETNET/OPERA radar operators; NASA GSFC SPDF OMNI2 (King and Papitashvili 2005) with Kp from GFZ Potsdam; Open-Meteo (CC BY 4.0) with ERA5 from the Copernicus Climate Change Service (Hersbach et al. 2020); INTERMAGNET observatories. No endorsement implied.
human_role: Directed the work, chose and approved the frozen designs and Amendment 1, followed the results and approved publication; did not line-edit the note.
ai_assistance: Substantial. Claude (Anthropic) wrote the analysis code, simulation and tests, ran the analyses, and drafted the plans, write-up, note and this record. AI review is not human peer review.

limitations: Kp is planetary and 3-hourly; the US study used local magnetometer disturbance (dBmax). The local check (INTERMAGNET) covers autumn only and approximates the US index.
100 m ERA5 wind stands in for flight-level wind; residual synoptic weather is the main rival explanation.
ln(VID + 0.1) attenuates multiplicative effects by about 12-14%; effect sizes compare to the US log10 reflectivity outcome only approximately.
23 autumn and 25 spring storm nights, clustered in episodes; one three-year window near solar maximum.
The freeze is self-attested: private git commits and local download logs, not a public registry.
Does not show that geomagnetic disturbance has no effect on European migration, nor that the US result is wrong.
